title: A cycle-usable exact-map quantity sees O/E order and is not already D_w, a named cell, or cheap-OOE adjacency
statement: There is a quantity Q of the exact ordered map T_w, for CycleMin-legal words with the same exponent budget (o, L), that is not a function of (o, L) alone and is not already lowerDenom / S(w), a named cell (OE / OOE / EOO), cheap-OOE adjacency, peak-valley composition, cyclic rounding, prefix expansion, or the CycleItinerary endpoint identities Delta = n^{3^o}-n^{2^L} and T/n^P = n^{1-P}.
counterexamples: on a CycleItinerary, Delta = n^{3^o}-n^{2^L} and T/n^P = n^{1-P} are functions of (n, o, L) only (global_defect_identity plus image_eq_start_defectRatio)
each n follows exactly one word of each length, so distinct same-length words have disjoint domains and cannot be compared at the same start
12 distinct expanding necklace pairs with the same (o, L) through length 8 all have different S and tag lowerDenom; unarchived=0
OOE / OEO / EOO share budget 9/8 and are one necklace excluded by named cells / rotation
OOOEE versus OOEOE share budget 27/32 and differ by the archived cheap-OOE then OE factor
notes: Phase 0 only. Complementary slogan to the closed exponent budget: the exact map sees letter order, and every cycle-usable compression is archived. Not a reopen of D_w, named cells, cheap-OOE adjacency, finance, or peak-valley composition. No K=11, no L=25781, no floor raise. No Paper A edit, no theorem-ledger row, no new Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: endpoint identities on (3, OOE/OEO), (5, OOE/EOO), (7, OOOEE/OOEOE), (11, OOOOE/OOOEO); expanding census k<=8 (105 words, 17 budgets, 12 necklace pairs) with follows scan on [2,2001); itinerary uniqueness n<64, k<=6
